sources.note: RFS-Guard detects and localizes reasoning hallucinations in LRMs training-free, using a Routing Focus Score (RFS) that measures how strongly cross-step attention between reasoning and answer phases collapses toward semantic-neighbor proximity (rather than task-critical evidence) -- finding this 'routing collapse' is a strong hallucination signal that beats sampling-based, uncertainty-based, and other self-aware baselines while remaining far more inference-efficient.
sources.title: RFS-Guard: Detecting Reasoning Hallucinations via Cross-Phase Routing Focus in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: A test-time-compute-allocation framework unifies where to spend compute (which unresolved queries get more sampling) with how generation is performed there (conditioning new samples on in-context demonstrations retrieved, via semantic similarity, from other queries already solved during the same inference run) -- consistently beating uniform Best-of-N and a difficulty-adaptive elimination baseline in coverage-per-token across four model families and multiple math/coding/reasoning benchmarks, with gains concentrated early in test-time scaling.
sources.title: Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation with Evolving In-Context Demonstrations
